title: HTML & CSS — Your First Web Page
description: Build a real web page from scratch. HTML is structure, CSS is style. Together they make everything you see on the web.

title: JavaScript in the Browser
description: Make your web page respond to users. Clicks, forms, dynamic content. This is where it gets fun.

title: Ship It — From Laptop to the Internet
description: Deploy your app. Buy a domain, set up hosting, go live. Your first URL that strangers can visit.

title: HTML: Structure and Meaning
description: Build a page whose structure describes what the content actually is — headings that form a real outline, lists that are really lists, and elements that tell a screen reader what something is before you've styled a single pixel of it.

title: CSS: Making It Look Right
description: Style a page deliberately — choosing what a rule targets on purpose, understanding why an element's size isn't what you typed, laying things out with flexbox, and making sure the result is actually readable, not just designed.

title: JavaScript in the Page
description: Make a page respond to what someone actually does — find and change an element, react to a click or a keypress, read what was typed into a form, and do all of it in a way that still works for a screen reader and a keyboard, not just a mouse.

title: Remembering Things
description: Save and reload data so a page remembers between visits — the browser's built-in string-only key-value store, JSON as the shape that gets real data in and out of it, and handling both the very first visit and a corrupted save without the page just breaking.

title: Getting Data From Elsewhere
description: Fetch data from an API and display it — what an API and an endpoint actually are, the request/response round trip, why the network doesn't answer instantly, and what still has to work correctly when the request fails, not just when it succeeds.
